_meta.title: SLATE research: intercity buses, local transit, rail cancellations, towns and hotels
_meta.method: Web research on 2026-09-29. Every figure carries a source URL, a date or period, and sourceType primary (operator/government/regulator) or secondary. Unconfirmable values are null and listed in uncertain. Figures derived by arithmetic from published data are labelled derived, not published.

notes: Every figure below was seen in the cited source during this session unless its note says otherwise.

US 'acsMeanTransitCommute' figures were COMPUTED here from two published ACS 2020-2024 5-year tables (aggregate travel time B08136_007 divided by worker count B08301_010, both 'Public transportation (excluding taxicab)'). That is the Census Bureau's own definition of the mean, but the quotient itself is not a printed figure. Values retrieved via the Census Reporter API because the Census API required a key.

Moovit figures are from Moovit's 2024 Global Public Transport Report (published Dec 2024): 'the average time it takes to commute one way' on public transit, derived from Moovit app trip requests plus user research. Metro-area level, not the city proper. Secondary in the sense of being a private company's app data.
UK DfT TSGB0111 (2024, published 17 Dec 2025) = Labour Force Survey, Oct-Dec 2024, average usual one-way time to travel to work, by REGION OF WORKPLACE and usual method, minutes.

amtrak.rebooking: 'Every reasonable effort will be made to rebook you on the next available service and to reroute your checked baggage on the same service'; no additional fees on rebooking/refunds for Amtrak schedule changes or cancellations.
amtrak.alternateTransport: In significant disruptions: other Amtrak trains, chartered or scheduled buses, or air when feasible.
amtrak.refund: Eligible unused tickets bought by credit card refunded to the original card within 14 days; tickets paid by eVoucher, gift card, check or cash refunded as an eVoucher. Where Amtrak cancels for events beyond its control, refund in original form of payment.
amtrak.compensation: Discretionary, not statutory: 'may be offered in the form of Amtrak Guest Rewards points, a Transportation Voucher, and/or a refund for the affected travel segment.' Hotel/food when an Amtrak-controlled disruption forces an overnight stay.
amtrak.fareAdjustmentRule: Normal rule that changes must be made before departure 'will not apply if there is a service disruption.'

uk_delay_repay.howCancellationsWork: A cancellation is compensated by the resulting delay at destination (e.g. taking the next train and arriving 60+ min late pays the 60-119 band). If you choose not to travel because of a delay or cancellation, the unused ticket is refunded with no fee by the original retailer.

lner.note: lner.co.uk/support/delay-repay returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches; bands confirmed via secondary sources (refundmyrail, myrailbuddy 'DR30') and consistent with the standard DR30 scheme.

eurostar.alternative: Bonus loyalty points instead of voucher/cash.
eurostar.claimWindow: 3 months to claim; e-vouchers redeemable within 12 months of the delay
eurostar.cancellation: Same information, help and compensation policy as delays; where cancellation means 60+ min late arrival the passenger may take a full refund for the affected journey if not travelling, or postpone to a later date/time.
eurostar.legalBasis: EU Regulation 2021/782 (cash floor 25% at 60 min, 50% at 120 min); Eurostar's voucher rates exceed it. UK leg is under the UK's retained version of EU rail passenger rights. Passenger-rights page: https://www.eurostar.com/us-en/rail-passengers-rights

irish_rail.euRule: Regulation (EU) 2021/782 Art. 19: minimum 25% of ticket price for 60-119 min delay, 50% for 120+ min; no payment below EUR 4.

irish_rail.cancellationOr60minDelay: Choose: full refund if journey abandoned before starting; refund of untravelled part if discontinued; or return to origin by train with full refund. Hotel and notification costs possibly covered if a missed connection strands you overnight.
